subject: math
title: Multiplying and Dividing Decimals
seo_title: Grade 7 Multiplying and Dividing Decimals Worksheets (Free, Ontario, Answer Key)
standard_text: Multiply and divide decimal numbers by decimal numbers, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing decimals by decimals for the Ontario curriculum: counting decimal places, estimating to place the decimal point, dividing by a decimal, mixed practice and word problems with gas prices and price per kilogram. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply or divide like whole numbers, then place the decimal point and check with an estimate.
key_sub: To multiply, add the decimal places: 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.06, not 0.6. To divide by a decimal, move both points the same number of places: 4.92 ÷ 0.12 = 492 ÷ 12 = 41.
body_html:
Work with whole numbers, then place the decimal point

To multiply or divide decimals, work as if there were no decimal points. Then use a rule to put the point in the right place, and check it with an estimate.

Multiply: count the decimal places

Add the number of decimal places in the two numbers. The answer has that many places. Count them before you drop any zeros at the end.

Example 1

2.35 × 1.4

235 × 14 = 3290. 2.35 has 2 decimal places and 1.4 has 1, so the answer has 3: 3.290 = 3.29. Estimate: 2 × 1.5 = 3.

Answer: 3.29

Divide by a decimal: move both points

Make the divisor a whole number. Move its decimal point to the right, then move the point in the dividend the same number of places. Write zeros if you need more places. Both numbers are multiplied by the same power of 10, so the answer does not change.

Example 2

3.6 ÷ 0.04

0.04 has 2 decimal places. Move both points 2 places, writing a zero in 3.6: 3.6 ÷ 0.04 = 360 ÷ 4 = 90. Check: 90 × 0.04 = 3.6.

Answer: 90

Estimate to check the point

Round to easy numbers. 5.9 × 4.2 is about 6 × 4 = 24, so the answer is 24.78, not 2.478 or 247.8. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes the answer smaller. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes it bigger.

Example 3

Gas costs $1.52 per litre. How much do 35.5 L cost?

355 × 152 = 53 960. Count 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places: 53.960. Estimate: 35 × $1.50 = $52.50.

Answer: $53.96

Example 4

A 0.35 kg piece of cheese costs $8.40. What is the price per kilogram?

Price per kilogram = cost ÷ mass. $8.40 ÷ 0.35 = 840 ÷ 35 = 24. Check: 0.35 × $24 = $8.40.

Answer: $24 per kilogram

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.3 × 0.2 = 0.61 + 1 = 2 decimal places: 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.06
Lining up the points to multiplyLine up on the right, then count the decimal places
0.8 × 0.5 = 0.04 (dropping the zero first)Count 2 places in 40 first: 0.40 = 0.4
5.25 ÷ 0.5 = 1.05 (moving the point only in the divisor)Move both points: 52.5 ÷ 5 = 10.5
3.6 ÷ 0.04 = 9 (moving the points different amounts)Move both 2 places: 360 ÷ 4 = 90
8.4 × 3.6 = 3.024 (point in the wrong place)Estimate 8 × 4 = 32, so the answer is 30.24

faq.q: What does the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum say about multiplying and dividing decimals?
faq.a: In Grade 7, students multiply and divide decimal numbers by decimal numbers, like 2.35 × 1.4 and 4.92 ÷ 0.12, in different contexts such as money and measurement. In Grade 6 they only worked with whole numbers and decimal tenths.

faq.q: Why is 0.3 × 0.2 equal to 0.06 and not 0.6?
faq.a: 0.3 × 0.2 means 3 tenths of 2 tenths, which is 6 hundredths. Both numbers have 1 decimal place, so the answer needs 2: 0.06. It must also be less than 0.2, and 0.6 is not.

faq.q: How do you divide a decimal by a decimal, like 4.92 ÷ 0.12?
faq.a: Move the decimal point in the divisor to make it a whole number, and move the point in the dividend the same number of places: 4.92 ÷ 0.12 = 492 ÷ 12 = 41. Check by multiplying: 41 × 0.12 = 4.92.

faq.q: Does multiplying by a decimal always make a number smaller?
faq.a: Only when the decimal is less than 1: 8 × 0.5 = 4. Multiplying by a decimal greater than 1 makes it bigger (8 × 1.5 = 12), and dividing by a decimal less than 1 makes it bigger (8 ÷ 0.5 = 16).

sets.title: Decimal × decimal: count the decimal places

items.q: The dark squares show 0.3 × 0.2. What is 0.3 × 0.2?
items.e: 3 tenths × 2 tenths = 6 hundredths: 6 of the 100 small squares are dark. 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.06. 0.6 is the common mistake: 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places, so the answer needs 2 places. 0.5 adds.

items.q: The dark squares show 0.6 × 0.4. What is 0.6 × 0.4?
items.e: 6 columns × 4 rows = 24 dark squares out of 100, so 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.24. The answer is less than both 0.6 and 0.4, so 2.4 cannot be right. 1 adds 0.6 + 0.4.

items.q: The dark squares show 0.8 × 0.5. What is 0.8 × 0.5?
items.e: 40 dark squares out of 100 is 0.40 = 0.4. 8 × 5 = 40, then count 2 places: 0.40. 0.04 drops the zero first and then counts 2 places: count before you drop zeros.

items.q: How many decimal places does the answer to 0.7 × 0.03 have?
items.e: 0.7 has 1 decimal place and 0.03 has 2. The product has 1 + 2 = 3 places: 7 × 3 = 21, so 0.7 × 0.03 = 0.021. 2 uses only the larger number of places.
Multiply as whole numbers: 7 × 3 = 21. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.021. 0.21 counts only 2 places.
Multiply as whole numbers: 4 × 9 = 36. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Count 2 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.36.
Multiply as whole numbers: 13 × 2 = 26. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Count 2 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.26.
Multiply as whole numbers: 24 × 3 = 72. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Count 2 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.72.
Multiply as whole numbers: 5 × 6 = 30. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.030 = 0.03.

items.q: Which product equals 0.48?
325 × 16 = 5200. Where does the decimal point go in 3.25 × 1.6?
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 325 × 16 = 5200. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 5.200 = 5.2. Estimate: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5, so 5.2 makes sense. 52 counts only 2 places.

items.q: 45 × 27 = 1215. What is 0.45 × 2.7?
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 45 × 27 = 1215. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 1.215. Estimate: half of 2.7 is about 1.35, so 1.215 makes sense.
Multiply as whole numbers: 46 × 35 = 1610. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 1.610 = 1.61.
Multiply as whole numbers: 12 × 8 = 96. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.096.
Multiply as whole numbers: 625 × 4 = 2500. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 2.500 = 2.5.
Multiply as whole numbers: 108 × 25 = 2700. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 2.700 = 2.7.
2 × 3 × 5 = 30. Each number has 1 decimal place, so the answer has 1 + 1 + 1 = 3: 0.030 = 0.03. 0.3 counts only 2 places. 1 adds the numbers.
3.7 has 1 decimal place and 0.54 has 2, so the product has 3: 1.998. Estimate: 4 × 0.5 = 2, which is close.

items.q: Without multiplying, which product is less than 0.6?
items.e: Compare the other number with 1. Only 0.9 is less than 1, so only 0.6 × 0.9 is less than 0.6 (it is 0.54). 0.6 × 1 is exactly 0.6.

items.q: Zoe says 0.8 × 0.7 = 5.6. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 8 × 7 = 56, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places, so 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56. Zoe counted only 1 place. Two numbers less than 1 have a product less than both of them.

sets.title: Estimate to place the decimal point

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 59.6 × 0.52?
items.e: 59.6 ≈ 60 and 0.52 ≈ 0.5. 60 × 0.5 = half of 60 = 30. 120 is 60 ÷ 0.5: it divides instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 63.7 ÷ 8.1?
items.e: 63.7 ≈ 64 and 8.1 ≈ 8. 64 ÷ 8 = 8. 56 is 64 − 8: it subtracts instead of dividing.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 3.02 × 5.9?
items.e: 3.02 ≈ 3 and 5.9 ≈ 6. 3 × 6 = 18. 9 is 3 + 6: it adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 0.99 × 74.2?
items.e: 0.99 is almost 1, and 1 × 74.2 = 74.2. So the answer is just under 74.2: about 74.

items.q: The digits of 5.9 × 4.2 are 2478. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 5.9 × 4.2?
items.e: Estimate: 6 × 4 = 24. Only 24.78 is close to that.

items.q: The digits of 46.8 ÷ 1.8 are 26. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 46.8 ÷ 1.8?
items.e: Estimate: 50 ÷ 2 = 25. Only 26 is close to that.

items.q: The digits of 18.9 ÷ 4.5 are 42. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 18.9 ÷ 4.5?
items.e: Estimate: 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Only 4.2 is close to that.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 7.2 ÷ 0.48?
items.e: 7.2 ≈ 7 and 0.48 ≈ 0.5. There are 2 halves in every whole, so 7 ÷ 0.5 = 14. (The exact answer is 15.) 3.5 is 7 × 0.5: it multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Nathan says 0.6 × 0.5 = 3. Which statement is true?
c: No: the answer must be less than 0.6
items.e: 0.5 is less than 1, so 0.6 × 0.5 is less than 0.6. 3 cannot be right. 6 × 5 = 30 and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places, so 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.30 = 0.3.

items.q: The digits of 152.1 ÷ 3.9 are 39. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 152.1 ÷ 3.9?
items.e: Estimate: 160 ÷ 4 = 40. Only 39 is close to that.

items.q: The digits of 7.92 ÷ 0.9 are 88. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 7.92 ÷ 0.9?
items.e: Estimate: 7.92 is about 8 and 0.9 is about 1, so the answer is about 8 ÷ 1 = 8 (a bit more, because 0.9 is less than 1). Only 8.8 is close to that.

items.q: The digits of 8.1 × 0.52 are 4212. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 8.1 × 0.52?
items.e: Estimate: 0.52 is about 0.5 (one half), and half of 8 is 4. Only 4.212 is close to that.

items.q: The digits of 0.48 × 0.6 are 288. Use an estimate to place the decimal point. What is 0.48 × 0.6?
items.e: Estimate: 0.48 is about 0.5, and half of 0.6 is 0.3. Only 0.288 is close to that.

items.q: Without dividing, which is true about 9.6 ÷ 0.8?
items.e: 0.8 is less than 1, so more than 9.6 groups of 0.8 fit into 9.6. The answer is greater than 9.6: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 = 96 ÷ 8 = 12.

items.q: Without multiplying, which product is greater than 5.6?
items.e: Only 1.1 is greater than 1, so only 5.6 × 1.1 is greater than 5.6 (it is 6.16). 5.6 × 1 is exactly 5.6, and 0.99 is just under 1.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 0.25 × 23.6?
items.e: 0.25 is one quarter. A quarter of 23.6 is about a quarter of 24 = 6 (exactly 5.9). 94 is about 23.6 ÷ 0.25: it divides instead of multiplying.

items.q: Without dividing, which quotient is less than 4.2?
items.e: Dividing by a number greater than 1 makes the answer smaller. Only 1.5 is greater than 1, so 4.2 ÷ 1.5 = 2.8 is less than 4.2. Dividing by 0.6 or 0.8 makes it bigger (7 and 5.25).

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 71.4 ÷ 9.8?
items.e: 71.4 ≈ 70 and 9.8 ≈ 10. 70 ÷ 10 = 7. 62 is about 71.4 − 9.8 = 61.6: it subtracts instead of dividing.

items.q: Mei works out 8.4 × 3.6 and gets 3.024. Use an estimate. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Estimate: 8 × 4 = 32, so the answer is about 30. 84 × 36 = 3024, and 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places: 30.24. Mei counted 3 places. 12 is the sum.

items.q: Arjun works out 16.8 ÷ 0.42 and gets 4. Use an estimate. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Estimate: 0.42 is about 0.4, and 16 ÷ 0.4 = 160 ÷ 4 = 40. Move both points 2 places: 16.8 ÷ 0.42 = 1680 ÷ 42 = 40. Arjun moved the point in 16.8 only 1 place (168 ÷ 42 = 4).

sets.title: Divide by a decimal: move both points

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 2.72 ÷ 0.17?
items.e: 0.17 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right. 2.72 ÷ 0.17 = 272 ÷ 17 = 16. Check: 16 × 0.17 = 2.72.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 9 ÷ 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right (write a zero in 9). 9 ÷ 0.6 = 90 ÷ 6 = 15. Check: 15 × 0.6 = 9.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 2.1 ÷ 0.35?
items.e: 0.35 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right (write a zero in 2.1). 2.1 ÷ 0.35 = 210 ÷ 35 = 6. Check: 6 × 0.35 = 2.1.

items.q: Both decimal points move the same number of places. What is 3.84 ÷ 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 3.84 ÷ 0.6 = 38.4 ÷ 6 = 6.4. Check: 6.4 × 0.6 = 3.84.

items.q: Which problem has the same answer as 8.46 ÷ 0.3?
items.e: 0.3 has 1 decimal place, so multiply both numbers by 10: 8.46 → 84.6 and 0.3 → 3. 8.46 ÷ 0.3 = 84.6 ÷ 3 = 28.2. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.
0.7 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 8.4 ÷ 0.7 = 84 ÷ 7 = 12. Check: 12 × 0.7 = 8.4.
3.2 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 19.2 ÷ 3.2 = 192 ÷ 32 = 6. Check: 6 × 3.2 = 19.2.

items.q: To find 2.85 ÷ 0.15, you multiply both numbers by the same number so the divisor is a whole number. Which number?
items.e: 0.15 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both by 100: 285 ÷ 15 = 19. × 10 gives 1.5, which is still a decimal. × 1000 also works but is more than you need.

items.q: Which problem has the same answer as 0.24 ÷ 0.008?
items.e: 0.008 has 3 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 1000: 0.24 → 240 and 0.008 → 8. 0.24 ÷ 0.008 = 240 ÷ 8 = 30. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.
1.7 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 4.25 ÷ 1.7 = 42.5 ÷ 17 = 2.5. Check: 2.5 × 1.7 = 4.25.
0.14 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right. 0.168 ÷ 0.14 = 16.8 ÷ 14 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 × 0.14 = 0.168.
0.6 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 0.42 ÷ 0.6 = 4.2 ÷ 6 = 0.7. Check: 0.7 × 0.6 = 0.42.

items.q: Which problem has the same answer as 15 ÷ 0.25?
items.e: 0.25 has 2 decimal places, so multiply both numbers by 100: 15 → 1500 and 0.25 → 25. 15 ÷ 0.25 = 1500 ÷ 25 = 60. Move the point the same number of places in both numbers.
0.48 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right (write zeros in 36). 36 ÷ 0.48 = 3600 ÷ 48 = 75. Check: 75 × 0.48 = 36.
0.12 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right (write a zero in 7.8). 7.8 ÷ 0.12 = 780 ÷ 12 = 65. Check: 65 × 0.12 = 7.8.

items.q: Emma wrote 5.25 ÷ 0.5 = 1.05. What mistake did she make?
c: She moved the point in both numbers
She moved the point only in 0.5
items.e: Emma changed 0.5 to 5 but left 5.25 as it was: 5.25 ÷ 5 = 1.05. She moved the point only in 0.5. Move both: 5.25 ÷ 0.5 = 52.5 ÷ 5 = 10.5.
0.8 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 43.2 ÷ 0.8 = 432 ÷ 8 = 54. Check: 54 × 0.8 = 43.2.
0.07 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right. 3.15 ÷ 0.07 = 315 ÷ 7 = 45. Check: 45 × 0.07 = 3.15.
0.012 has 3 decimal places, so move both decimal points 3 places to the right (write zeros in 5.4). 5.4 ÷ 0.012 = 5400 ÷ 12 = 450. Check: 450 × 0.012 = 5.4.

items.q: Why does 6.72 ÷ 0.24 have the same answer as 672 ÷ 24?
items.e: 6.72 × 100 = 672 and 0.24 × 100 = 24. When both numbers are multiplied by 100, the answer does not change, just as 6 ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 20 = 3. Both give 28.

sets.title: Mixed practice: multiply and divide decimals

items.e: Multiply as whole numbers: 9 × 4 = 36. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.036.
0.6 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 1.44 ÷ 0.6 = 14.4 ÷ 6 = 2.4. Check: 2.4 × 0.6 = 1.44.

items.q: Which words give the value of 0.3 × 0.2?
items.e: Tenths × tenths = hundredths (like 1/10 of 1/10 = 1/100). 3 × 2 = 6, so 0.3 × 0.2 = 6 hundredths = 0.06. 6 tenths (0.6) is the common mistake. 5 tenths adds.
Multiply as whole numbers: 26 × 15 = 390. Count the decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3. Count 3 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.390 = 0.39.
0.9 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 0.072 ÷ 0.9 = 0.72 ÷ 9 = 0.08. Check: 0.08 × 0.9 = 0.072.
Multiply as whole numbers: 25 × 36 = 900. Count the decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4. Count 4 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.0900 = 0.09.
0.035 has 3 decimal places, so move both decimal points 3 places to the right (write zeros in 12.6). 12.6 ÷ 0.035 = 12 600 ÷ 35 = 360. Check: 360 × 0.035 = 12.6.
The missing number is 2.6 × 0.5 = 1.3. Check: 1.3 ÷ 0.5 = 13 ÷ 5 = 2.6. 5.2 divides 2.6 ÷ 0.5 instead of multiplying.
Multiply as whole numbers: 48 × 125 = 6000. Count the decimal places: 1 + 3 = 4. Count 4 places from the right (write zeros in front to make room): 0.6000 = 0.6.
0.09 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right. 0.81 ÷ 0.09 = 81 ÷ 9 = 9. Check: 9 × 0.09 = 0.81.
The answer 0.6 is less than 1.2, so the missing number is less than 1. 0.6 ÷ 1.2 = 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5. 2 is 1.2 ÷ 0.6, the wrong way round.

items.q: Which multiplication checks that 2.08 ÷ 0.4 = 5.2?
items.e: Quotient × divisor = dividend. 5.2 × 0.4 = 2.08, so the division is right. 5.2 × 4 = 20.8 forgets that the divisor is 0.4.
Multiply as whole numbers: 705 × 6 = 4230. Count the decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3. Count 3 places from the right: 4.230 = 4.23.
1.3 has 1 decimal place, so move both decimal points 1 place to the right. 1.95 ÷ 1.3 = 19.5 ÷ 13 = 1.5. Check: 1.5 × 1.3 = 1.95.
Multiply as whole numbers: 35 × 28 = 980. Count the decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2. Count 2 places from the right: 9.80 = 9.8.
0.39 has 2 decimal places, so move both decimal points 2 places to the right (write a zero in 11.7). 11.7 ÷ 0.39 = 1170 ÷ 39 = 30. Check: 30 × 0.39 = 11.7.
Work from left to right. 2.4 ÷ 0.6 = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Then 4 × 0.5 = 2. 8 multiplies first: 2.4 ÷ 0.3. 0.2 moves the point only in 0.6 (2.4 ÷ 6 = 0.4, then 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2). 4 stops after one step.

items.q: Kai says 3.6 ÷ 0.04 = 9. What is the correct answer?
items.e: 0.04 has 2 decimal places, so move both points 2 places. 3.6 needs a zero: 3.60 → 360. 360 ÷ 4 = 90. Kai moved the point in 3.6 only 1 place (36 ÷ 4 = 9). Check: 90 × 0.04 = 3.6.

sets.title: Word problems: gas prices and price per kilogram

items.q: Gas costs $1.45 per litre in Ottawa. Liam’s mom buys 40 L. How much does she pay?
Old cheddar costs $18.50 per kilogram. Maya buys 0.4 kg. How much does it cost?
items.e: 185 × 4 = 740. $18.50 has 2 decimal places and 0.4 has 1, so count 3 places: 7.400 = $7.40. Estimate: 0.4 is less than half, and half of $18.50 is about $9. $18.90 adds.

items.q: Ground beef costs $12.80 per kilogram. Noah’s dad buys 1.5 kg for a barbecue. How much does he pay?
During a snowstorm in Barrie, 1.8 cm of snow fell every hour for 6.5 hours. How much snow fell in all?
Gas costs $1.50 per litre. How many litres can you buy for $60?
A 2.5 kg bag of Ontario apples costs $8.75. What is the price per kilogram?
Gas costs $1.52 per litre in Sudbury. Priya’s aunt pumps 35.5 L. How much does the gas cost?
items.e: 355 × 152 = 53 960. Count 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places: 53.960 = $53.96. Estimate: 35 × $1.50 = $52.50. $539.60 counts only 2 places. $37.02 adds.

items.q: A sugar shack pours 4.5 L of maple syrup into bottles that hold 0.25 L each. How many bottles does it fill?
Which is the better buy for carrots?
c: They cost the same per kilogram
items.e: Find the price per kilogram. $3.30 ÷ 1.5 = $2.20 per kilogram. $5.25 ÷ 2.5 = $2.10 per kilogram. 2.5 kg for $5.25 costs less per kilogram.

items.q: A 0.35 kg piece of Gouda costs $8.40. What is the price per kilogram?
items.e: $8.40 ÷ 0.35 = 840 ÷ 35 = $24 per kilogram. Check: 0.35 × $24 = $8.40. $0.24 moves the point only in 0.35. $2.94 multiplies.

items.q: Ethan’s dad pays $62.64 for 43.5 L of gas. What is the price per litre?
items.e: Price per litre = cost ÷ litres: 62.64 ÷ 43.5 = 626.4 ÷ 435 = $1.44. Check: 43.5 × $1.44 = $62.64. $19.14 subtracts and $106.14 adds.

items.q: Owen’s sister earns $17.60 per hour at a bakery in London, Ontario. She works 4.5 hours on Saturday. How much does she earn?
A family hikes a 10.8 km trail in Algonquin Park at 2.4 km per hour. How many hours does the hike take?
Gas costs $1.48 per litre. Which is the best estimate of the cost of 51.2 L?
items.e: $1.48 ≈ $1.50 and 51.2 L ≈ 50 L. 50 × $1.50 = $75. (The exact cost is $75.78 after rounding to the cent.) $52.68 adds 51.2 + 1.48.

items.q: Hana cuts 6.3 m of ribbon into pieces that are 0.45 m long for a class project. How many pieces does she get?
A car uses 0.075 L of gas per kilometre. The drive from Toronto to Ottawa is about 450 km. How much gas does the car use?
Leah’s family drives 486 km to a cottage near Sault Ste. Marie and uses 40.5 L of gas. How many kilometres do they drive per litre?
items.e: Kilometres per litre = km ÷ L: 486 ÷ 40.5 = 4860 ÷ 405 = 12 km. Estimate: 480 ÷ 40 = 12. 445.5 subtracts.

items.q: Grapes cost $4.40 per kilogram. Ava pays $5.94 for a bunch. How many kilograms of grapes does she buy?
items.e: Kilograms = cost ÷ price per kilogram: 5.94 ÷ 4.4 = 59.4 ÷ 44 = 1.35 kg. Check: 1.35 × $4.40 = $5.94. 1.54 subtracts 5.94 − 4.40.

items.q: Gas costs $1.39 per litre. Kai’s grandpa buys 35 L and pays with three $20 bills. How much change does he get?
items.e: Cost: 35 × $1.39 = $48.65. Change: $60 − $48.65 = $11.35. $48.65 is the cost, not the change. $12.65 subtracts only the dollars (60 − 48) and keeps the 65¢. $23.61 subtracts 35 and 1.39 from 60 instead of multiplying first.

items.q: At a farmers’ market, cherries cost $8.50 per kilogram and blueberries cost $11.25 per kilogram. Sofia buys 1.2 kg of cherries and 0.8 kg of blueberries. How much does she pay?
items.e: Cherries: 1.2 × $8.50 = $10.20. Blueberries: 0.8 × $11.25 = $9. Total: $10.20 + $9 = $19.20. $19.75 adds the two prices. $10.20 forgets the blueberries.
